title: Visual Studio Code on macOS saves this document by truncating and rewriting the same object

provenance.fixture: Before each run, <root>/doc.txt contained exactly `alpha original document\n`. The driver opened that file in a fresh VS Code profile, discovered that owned child through its OS-assigned loopback DevToolsActivePort, validated the real document editor, typed `VS Code edit: `, invoked Cmd-S and rejected any final bytes other than `VS Code edit: alpha original document\n`.
provenance.evidence: Three independent fresh-profile runs each exited 0 and produced the same three readings. `doc.txt` at inode 223462352 was 24 bytes at baseline, the SAME inode was observed at 0 bytes, and the SAME inode was then observed at 38 bytes. No temporary path appeared in any reading and the final bytes were checked after every save.
provenance.surprise: The existing `vscode-atomic-replace` supplement inferred a .vsctmp rename from a shipped binary helper. The real document-save path measured here did not use that shape: it exposed an in-place truncation on this host. The observed result wins for this matrix cell; the binary derivation remains supplementary evidence for a path or configuration that was not exercised.
blind_spots: open, flush, fsync and close are invisible to polling
a temporary created and removed entirely between two readings would be missed, but the unchanged inode proves that no temporary replaced doc.txt

objects.role: doc.txt, the document — one identity throughout

folder.fidelity: a backend that does not declare ObserveDurableBoundary
folder.omission_note: If truncation and rewrite complete between two readings, the folder backend sees one Written and skips the unsafe empty state. If it catches both, only quiescence distinguishes the final rewrite.

expected.meaningful_durable_change: doc.txt holds the exact edited text in the same object identity. The zero-length intermediate state is not a meaningful save.
expected.forbidden_note: Mount sequence 2 and folder sequence 1 are the zero-length state observed in every repetition. A checkpoint there would turn one ordinary VS Code save into a durable empty document.

notes: The observed GUI result is deliberately separate from `vscode-atomic-replace`; one is a measured document save on this host, the other is a binary-derived supplement.
On a mount, Closed anchors the meaningful boundary. On a folder backend, only established settling can close the window after the rewrite.
